search_keyword: turn of month effect stock returns strategy rules first last trading days
page_summary: TapeScript blog on the turn-of-the-month (Ultimo) effect, citing Ariel (1987) and McConnell & Xu (2008, Financial Analysts Journal): from 1926-2005 essentially all of the US stock markets average positive return occurred in a 4-trading-day window per month -- the last trading day of the month plus the first three trading days of the next month. Rest of month averaged near zero. Confirmed across 34 other countries. Driven by predictable month-end cash flows (paychecks, 401k contributions, fund rebalancing).
notes: Concrete, parameter-light calendar-anomaly hypothesis: long only during last trading day of month + first N trading days of next month, flat otherwise. Testable directly on SPY/QQQ (equity) and BTC/USDT/ETH/USDT (crypto, to see if a cash-flow-driven equity effect transfers to a market without payroll/401k cycles).

notes: Adapted the daily-granularity-testable core of the academic finding: after a gap DOWN (open meaningfully below prior close), go long from open to close (intraday only), betting on a fade/reversal back up -- long-only per SAFETY.md, so only testing the gap-down-fade side (would require shorting to fade gap-ups). Two strategy families documented: (1) pullback-reversal (needs trend line + candlestick pattern + oscillator divergence, subjective/discretionary, similar implementability issue as RSI-divergence -019); (2) pivot-level breakout (concrete, mechanical): wait for price to CLOSE above/below a pivot level (P, R1, R2, R3, S1, S2, S3) signaling a new trend emerging, go long/short accordingly, stop beyond the next pivot level, target at 2:1 R:R.
notes: Implementing the mechanically-testable breakout variant (close crosses above the DAILY pivot point P, computed from the prior day's H/L/C, signals a long entry; exit when close crosses back below P) rather than the discretionary pullback-reversal variant. First Pivot Point (classic floor-trader P/R/S levels derived from prior-session HLC) strategy tested in this repo -- distinct from every prior indicator since it uses NO smoothing/lookback window at all, purely the single prior bar's H/L/C algebraically combined.

Volume Zone Oscillator (VZO, Khalil & Steckler 2009/2011): VZO = 100*(VP/TV) where TV=n-day EMA(volume), VP=n-day EMA(signed volume, OBV-style +/- based on close vs prior close). Zone levels: 5/20/40/60% and negative counterparts. Free explicit rule: combine with ADX(14)>18 trend filter + 60-period EMA direction filter. Trend Intensity Index (TII, M.H. Pee, Stocks & Commodities June 2002): major MA period (default 60, SMA of close) and minor period (default 30). For each of the last `minor` bars, deviation from the major MA is computed; positive deviations summed (SDPOS), negative deviations summed (SDNEG). TII = 100*SDPOS/(SDPOS+SDNEG), range 0-100, midline=50. Used as a midline-cross confirmation indicator (TII crossing above 50 = bullish confirmation, below 50 = bearish) rather than a classic overbought/oversold oscillator. Random Walk Index (RWI) formula: RWI High = (n-day High - n-day Low) / (ATR(n) * n); analogous RWI Low uses the inverse direction. Values above 0.5 = trend initiation, above 1.0 = strong trend. Crossover rule: bullish signal when RWI High crosses above RWI Low from below; bearish when RWI High crosses below RWI Low. Values near 0 = ranging/directionless market. search_keyword: Kaufman Adaptive Moving Average KAMA trading strategy crossover entry exit rules
page_summary: ArrowAlgo KAMA guide (Perry Kaufman, 1995). Formula: Efficiency Ratio ER = |close - close[n periods ago]| / sum(|close[i]-close[i-1]|) over n bars; Smoothing Constant SC = (ER*(fast_sc-slow_sc)+slow_sc)^2 where fast_sc=2/(2+1), slow_sc=2/(30+1); KAMA[t] = KAMA[t-1] + SC*(close[t]-KAMA[t-1]). Strategies: (1) trend-following via KAMA slope -- long when KAMA slopes upward and price above it, exit when KAMA flattens/slopes down; (2) dual KAMA crossover (fast n=10 vs slow n=20); (3) price/KAMA crossover. Recommends 15min+ timeframes, default n=10 with fast=2/slow=30.
notes: First KAMA strategy in this repo -- distinct from other adaptive/smoothing MAs (ZLEMA, VWMA, T3, Hull already tested) since KAMA's smoothing constant is dynamically derived from an efficiency ratio of trend-vs-noise, not a fixed weighting scheme.

search_keyword: Vertical Horizontal Filter VHF indicator trend strength trading strategy rules

Formula: VHF_n = (max(close, n) - min(close, n)) / sum(|close[i]-close[i-1]| for i in n) -- net directional distance over cumulative path traveled. Higher VHF = more efficient/trending; lower = choppy/ranging. Does NOT indicate direction, only trend strength -- pair with a directional signal (SMA/trendline/momentum). Rising VHF = breakout has better structural support; falling/flat VHF = lower odds of follow-through. Common lookbacks 14-30, daily-chart sweet spot ~28.
notes: First VHF strategy in this repo. Distinct from ADX (already tested, similar trend-strength-not-direction concept but different formula basis: ADX uses directional movement +DI/-DI, VHF uses raw close range vs cumulative path).

page_summary: LightningChart RWI explainer (Michael Poulos). Compares actual price movement to a random-walk null hypothesis over n periods using ATR-normalized range: RWI High = (High - Low(n periods ago)) / (ATR(n)*sqrt(n)), RWI Low = (High(n periods ago) - Low) / (ATR(n)*sqrt(n)). Interpretation: RWI High > 1.0 and RWI Low < 1.0 signals a statistically-significant uptrend; RWI Low > 1.0 and RWI High < 1.0 signals downtrend; both < 1.0 = random/noise (no tradeable trend). Common threshold 1.0-1.5, common period n=14.
notes: First Random Walk Index strategy in this repo -- distinct from VHF/ADX/Choppiness Index (already tested, all trend-strength-not-direction concepts) since RWI directly compares to a statistical random-walk null hypothesis rather than a raw range-vs-path ratio.

summary: DeMarker (DeM) indicator by Thomas DeMark: DeMax=max(high-high[1],0), DeMin=max(low[1]-low,0), DeM=SMA(DeMax,n)/(SMA(DeMax,n)+SMA(DeMin,n)) scaled 0-1 (or 0-100), default n=14. >0.7 overbought/exhaustion, <0.3 oversold/exhaustion; used for reversal/exhaustion signals, often combined with trend filter.

Hurst exponent (R/S rescaled-range analysis) H in (0,1): H>0.5 = persistent/trending behavior (momentum indicators favored), H<0.5 = anti-persistent/mean-reverting (RSI-style indicators favored), H~0.5 = random walk (no exploitable structure). Rolling H over a sliding window creates a time-varying regime indicator. No concrete strategy backtest given, but clear regime-classification rule.

StockSpotter's own threshold convention: BUYZONE=+50, SELLZONE=-50 (smoothed PFE crossing above 50 = buy signal, below -50 = sell signal). First PFE strategy in this repo.

Full free disclosure of Trend Trigger Factor (TTF, M.H. Pee, TASC Dec 2004) formula and rule: buy_power_n = HighestHigh(days 1-n)/LowestLow(days n+1-2n); sell_power_n = HighestHigh(days n+1-2n)/LowestLow(days 1-n); TTF = 100*(buy_power-sell_power)/(0.5*(buy_power+sell_power)). Default n=8. Zero-line-cross mechanical rule: TTF crossing above zero = long entry (next bar open); crossing below zero = short/exit signal. Optional t3-smoothing (period=3) and bottomline extremes (+/-75) noted but not required for the base rule. TradingView listing for Andean Oscillator (alexgrover, Jul 2022): bull component (green) = rising bullish price variation, bear component (red) = rising bearish; when bull>bear market is up-trending, bear>bull down-trending. Signal line (orange, EMA of the indicator) can filter false crossover signals -- source suggests entering when bull/bear crosses ABOVE the signal line rather than on the raw bull/bear cross. Built from exponential envelopes (upper/lower extremity trackers) plus squared-price envelopes for a naive-variance-style spread estimate.

Alpaca's own blog post (original publication source) detailing Andean Oscillator's construction: exponential envelopes (upper/lower extremities via online recursive max/min-with-decay, similar to but distinct from EMA) applied to both raw and squared close/open prices; bull component = sqrt(squared-lower-extremity - lower-extremity^2), bear component = sqrt(squared-upper-extremity - upper-extremity^2) (naive rolling-variance-style spread estimate, online/serial computation suitable for HFT). Signal line = EMA of max(bull,bear). First Andean Oscillator strategy in this repo -- a novel (2022) online-algorithm-based trend indicator distinct from all prior Keltner/Bollinger-envelope or classic-MA-crossover constructions already tested.

Bollinger Band Walk (Trend Following) strategy, concrete rules: Setup = price breaks out above resistance/squeeze, first candle closes above upper band, middle band (20 SMA) slopes in trend direction, volume above average, RSI>60 (bullish) or <40 (bearish). Entry rule: do NOT chase price on the outer band -- wait for the FIRST PULLBACK to the middle band (20 SMA) after the band walk begins, enter there (ADX>25 confirms trend). Stop: below middle band (0.2-0.3% for large caps). Target: upper band first, then trail stop below middle band. Exit: when price closes below the middle band (band walk is over). Distinct from all standalone BB mean-reversion/squeeze/percent-B strategies already tested in this repo -- this is a pullback-to-basis entry during an established band-walk trend, not a band-touch or squeeze-release entry.

RSI Range-Momentum strategy (per Arthur Hill paper 'Finding consistent trends with strong momentum'): uses RSI as a MOMENTUM (not mean-reversion) signal over a 100-day lookback with RSI(14). RSI Bull Range = RSI fluctuated between 40-100 over trailing 100 days. RSI Bull Momentum = highest RSI value over trailing 100 days exceeded 70. Source's own SPY backtest (1993-present): CAGR 5.93% vs buy-hold 9.58%, 35.7% time in market, 12 trades, 83% win rate, MDD 12.9%. Weis Wave Volume (WWV, David Weis, 1990s VSA technique): accumulates volume during each directional price wave (resets when consecutive-close direction flips, trendDetectionLength=2 default), unlike cumulative OBV. Page gives 3 concrete strategies: (1) Accumulation Breakout -- 3+ up-waves with growing volume exceeding intervening down-waves, entry on swing-high breakout with wave volume >=1.5x prior up-wave; (2) Climax Reversal -- entry opposite direction after a wave with volume >=2x the 3-wave average; (3) Wave Volume + 200 EMA trend filter -- only take accumulation(up-wave volume growing) signals when close>EMA200, distribution signals when close<EMA200. Concrete, testable, distinct from OBV/Klinger/VPCI/PVO already in this repo since it is wave-segmented (resets per directional wave) not cumulative or EMA-difference based.

David Varadi Oscillator (DVO) full formula disclosed: (1) ratio = Close / MedianPrice (MedianPrice=(High+Low)/2), (2) detrended = SMA(ratio, n) [n-period simple moving average smooths the ratio, removing trend influence per Varadi own stated rationale -- comparable to RSI but on detrended cyclical swings rather than raw price], (3) DVO = 100*PercentRank(detrended, lookback) [rolling percentile rank of the detrended series over lookback bars, 0-100 range]. Page states DVO like RSI is meant to buy pullback swings in an uptrend and sell impulse-swing tops in a downtrend, oscillating 0-100 (low=oversold swing, high=overbought swing). Exact numeric trading rules/AmiBroker code are paywalled (members-only section), but the formula plus RSI-analog interpretation (low DVO=buy-the-dip signal, high DVO=sell-the-rally signal) gives a concrete testable construction: long when DVO crosses above an oversold threshold from below, exit on DVO reaching an overbought threshold or time-stop.

Standard Error Bands (SEB): rolling linear regression centerline +/- N standard errors of the regression (not std dev like Bollinger). Trend-continuation strategy: when the regression line slopes up (uptrend) and price pulls back to the regression centerline (not the band extreme), buy; ride until regression slope flattens/reverses. Recommended settings period=20, deviations=2.0 daily. Used as basis for SEB regression-pullback trend-continuation strategy this iteration -- new indicator family, first regression-based band construction distinct from Bollinger/Keltner/Donchian already tested.

Kalman filter trading strategy overview: prediction/update recursive state estimation. 'Trend Estimation' implementation: single Kalman filter produces a smooth adaptive trend line (less lag than fixed-period MA); when actual price crosses above the Kalman trend line, bullish signal (opposite for bearish). Distinct from already-tested 2026-09-05-056 (dual fast/slow Kalman filter percentile-breakout construction) -- this is a single-filter price/trend-line crossover, simpler and more direct signal. Return skewness formula: Skew = [n/((n-1)(n-2))] * sum(((r_i-mean)/std)^3). Positive skew = frequent small losses, occasional large gains (right tail heavy) -- structurally matches trend-following payoff profile. Negative skew = frequent small gains, occasional large losses (left tail heavy) -- matches mean-reversion/option-selling payoff profile. Rolling skewness detects regime shifts in this asymmetry over time. No explicit trading rule given, but the mapping (positive-skew regime suits trend-following, negative-skew regime suits mean-reversion) is a standard quant heuristic. Used as basis for a rolling-skewness regime-gated trend-following strategy this iteration -- new indicator family, first skewness-based construction in this repo (0 prior 'skewness'/'skew' hits beyond incidental mentions).

Oscillates around zero. Source's stated trend-continuation strategy: pullback to a key level in an uptrend + REX crossing back to positive = long entry; primarily described as an EXIT signal (bearish reversal in uptrend = REX crosses negative). William O'Neil's Follow-Through Day (FTD) market-timing criteria: rally attempt day 1 = first up-close after a new correction low; FTD confirms on the attempt's 4th-7th day with an index gain of 1.5-2%+ on higher volume; distribution days (down days on higher volume) warn of rally failure. Coppock Curve: WMA(ROC(close,11)+ROC(close,14),10) on MONTHLY bars. Long entry when curve crosses above zero, exit when crosses below zero. Source backtest (S&P500, monthly, since 1960): 12 trades, 100% win rate, avg gain 45%/trade, annual return 6.11% vs buy-hold 7.03%, invested 73.75% of time, max drawdown 30.16% vs buy-hold 52.56%. Psychological Line (PSY): % of up-close bars (close>prior close) over N periods (0-100 scale). Above 50=bullish, below 50=bearish. Overbought>70 (reversal down likely), oversold<30 (reversal up likely). Also supports trend-following (trade with >50/<50) or divergence variants. First PSY strategy candidate for this repo -- distinct from RSI/Stochastic (uses simple up/down bar COUNT not magnitude).

Trend Intensity Index (TII): counts days price is above vs below a moving average (SMA) over lookback period, 0-100 scale. >80=strong uptrend, <20=strong downtrend, 50=no trend. Directional (unlike ADX) and faster to respond. Specific strategy: TII(30)/SMA(50)/ATR(14). Entry: long when TII crosses above 80 AND price above 50SMA. Exit: TII crosses back below 50, or 1.5xATR trailing stop. Backtested on 64 futures symbols, mixed results (PF 0.18-2.5, some negative Sharpe). First TII strategy candidate for this repo.

TD Sequential (DeMark): counts consecutive closes above/below close 4 bars prior. 9-count Setup = exhaustion signal; 13-count Countdown = stronger reversal confirmation (requires close<=low[2] bars prior, cumulative). Entry: counter-trend when 9-Setup completes with bar8/9 closing beyond bar6/7; 13-Countdown is a STRONGER signal than Setup alone. Exit: target opposite-direction TD Setup, stop beyond extreme of completed setup, hold 1-4 bars min. Source 64-futures-symbol backtest shows highly mixed results by instrument (Sharpe -0.67 to 2.50). Distinct from already-tested simple 9-count-only TD Setup (2026-09-04-032, rejected) via the additional 13-count Countdown confirmation layer.

CVR3 VIX Market Timing (Larry Connors & Dave Landry): trades SPY based on VIX behavior relative to its own 10-day MA. BUY signal (long SPY): VIX daily low > VIX 10d MA AND VIX close >=10% above 10d MA (PPO(1,10,1)>=10) AND VIX close<open (down candle). SELL/short signal (mirror): VIX high<10d MA AND VIX close<=10% below 10d MA AND VIX close>open. Stop-loss: exit long when VIX crosses back below the PRIOR days 10d MA, or a 2-4 day time exit. First VIX-timing strategy tested using actual VIX index data (loadable via yfinance ^VIX ticker) -- distinct from all prior volatility-PROXY strategies (WVF/Williams VIX Fix, ATR-based) which synthesize a fear proxy from price alone rather than using the real VIX.

Lo-MacKinlay (1988) Variance Ratio Test: VR(k)=Var(k-period return)/(k*Var(1-period return)). VR=1 random walk (no edge), VR<1 mean-reverting (negative autocorrelation, favors market-making/pairs), VR>1 trending/momentum (positive autocorrelation, favors trend-following/breakout). Gives full formula and reference Python implementation with homoscedastic z-stat. Used to build a VR(k) trending-regime gate for a trend-following EMA crossover strategy.

Stop below the pattern low, confirmation on 5th candle optional. Used to build Three Line Strike reversal strategy.

CPPI (Constant Proportion Portfolio Insurance): floor=protected minimum value, cushion=portfolio_value-floor, risky allocation=multiplier*cushion. Kelly formula f*=(bp-q)/b (p=win rate, q=1-p, b=avg win/avg loss). Full Kelly produces 50-80% drawdowns even with positive edge; fractional Kelly (25-50% of full) captures ~75% of growth at ~half the drawdown. Quarter Kelly materially calmer. Entry at D inside PRZ on reversal confirmation, stop beyond the extreme completion limit, scale-out targets at C/B/A/X retracement levels. Buy signal: Strong Ratio crosses above Weak Ratio; sell/exit: Weak Ratio crosses above Strong Ratio, or an extreme-then-turning-down reading signals momentum exhaustion.

Exact formula: for each of the last Period days, classify as up-day if typical_price[t] > typical_price[t-1] + 0.1*ATR(Period), down-day if typical_price[t] < typical_price[t-1] - 0.1*ATR(Period); Vp=sum(volume on up days), Vn=sum(volume on down days), Vtotal=sum(all volume); VPN = EMA(100*(Vp-Vn)/Vtotal, 3). Source's own simplified single-asset buy rule: VPN crosses over threshold (10%) AND 50-day vol avg rising AND RSI(5)<90 AND price>SMA(30); sell: VPN crosses below its own 30-day SMA while price >3 ATR below 5-day high, or fixed 15-day lifetime. search_keyword: Chaikin Oscillator divergence strategy
page_summary: ForexMT4Indicators Chaikin Oscillator Hidden Trend Divergence strategy: trend continuation (not reversal) system. Trend/pullback zone defined by 30 SMA and 50 SMA (uptrend when 30>50 and price above both). Buy: price pulls back into the 30/50 SMA band, bounces with a bullish momentum candle, AND that bounce coincides with a bullish HIDDEN divergence on the Chaikin Oscillator (price makes a higher low while Chaikin Osc makes a lower low -- confirms trend continuation rather than reversal). Counterattack Lines: 2-candle reversal pattern. Bullish version (in a downtrend): large bearish candle1, then candle2 opens lower (often gap-down) but rallies to close near candle1's close (a 'counterattack' matching close, not a full engulf). Bearish version (in an uptrend): large bullish candle1, then candle2 opens higher (gap-up) but sells off to close near candle1's close. Key distinguishing feature vs Engulfing pattern: the closes MATCH/are near-equal rather than one candle's body engulfing the other's. Used as source for this iteration's bullish-side long-only hypothesis (first Counterattack Lines strategy in this repo).

FRAMA (Fractal Adaptive Moving Average, John Ehlers) exact formula: D=(log(N1+N2)-log(N3))/log(2); alpha=clip(exp(-4.6*(D-1)), alpha_min, 1); F_t=alpha*P_t+(1-alpha)*F_(t-1). N1/N2/N3 are normalized high-low ranges over the first-half, second-half, and full lookback window respectively (standard Ehlers convention, confirmed via forexmt4indicators.com calculator cross-reference). Alpha adapts dynamically: low fractal dimension D (smooth/trending price) -> higher alpha -> more responsive; high D (choppy/noisy) -> lower alpha -> more smoothing. First FRAMA strategy in this repo (0 prior entries) -- distinct from KAMA (efficiency-ratio-based adaptive smoothing, already tested) via its fractal-dimension-based alpha derivation.
